text:
catie: Customer reported widespread 504s and 5xxs hitting /v1/generate during a sudden traffic surge at ~2026-03-15T12:34Z. They attached request_ids and sample times. Saying it lasts ~3-6 minutes. Escalating to incidents.
marisa: acknowledging, putting oncall in loop. Any immediate mitigations? :eyes:
shiv: initial glance looks like scale-up lag. KEDA scaledobject shows scaledReplicaCount jump but new pods stayed in `ContainerCreating`/`warmup` longer than readiness threshold. Repro logs attached below.
catie: attaching customer trace: request_id=req_0a12bc, gateway timed out after 30s, backend returned 502s intermittently.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T12:10 UTC to prod-redwood-completed (sha: a1b2c3). No config changes to HPA/KEDA in that deploy.
shiv: paste of readiness logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:34:05Z] model-init: loading weights... step 3/7
[2026-03-15T12:34:11Z] prewarm: failed healthcheck: timeout waiting for kv-cache init
[2026-03-15T12:34:15Z] readiness-probe: non-200 response for /live -> 503
[2026-03-15T12:34:20Z] container: marked Unready, will retry probe
```
marisa: hm KV cache init again. Any infra/errors in node events? kevin can you check kube events and node pressure?
kevin: checked nodes in that AZ. No memory pressure, but `docker` showed bursts of file-descriptor exhaustion on kubelet side. Also saw auth token refresh failures around 12:33 for the model-fetch service -> transient 403s from model registry (billing token rotation occurred at 12:32).
catie: customer mentioned a billing window earlier today. Could that have rotated tokens and triggered model-fetch retries that prolong warmup?
shiv: yes plausible: model-fetch retry loop blocks init, readiness fails, pod stays unready and HPA thinks capacity is low so KEDA adds more scaledObjects, creating a feedback loop. KEDA poll interval was 30s and cooldown 60s (config snippet below).
```
scaledObject:
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 60
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 8
```
marisa: so during surge we spawn more pods but they all hang during warm init because model fetch was rate-limited/403, so load backs up and gateway times out -> 504s. Steps?
shiv: immediate mitigation: 1) temporarily route burst traffic to a smaller lower-capacity model variant (less model-fetch overhead) or enable cached model snapshot. 2) increase readiness timeout and prewarm concurrency so pods have more time to initialize during burst. 3) reduce KEDA aggressiveness to avoid thundering herd (increase pollingInterval to 60s for now). 4) patch model-fetch to fail fast on auth 403 to avoid long retry loops.
kevin: I've opened a ticket with billing to confirm token rotation timeline and to get a rollback window. If billing team re-issued tokens mid-surge we should add a short-lived token fallback.
catie: customer communication: sending interim note that we're investigating scale-up warmup and auth interaction, will follow up with timeline and mitigation.
marisa: can we get exact repro steps to simulate? Shiv, can you write a repro harness? Keep it quick.
shiv: yep. Repro steps outline: 1) force token rotate or make /model-registry return 403 for 90s, 2) blast traffic with synthetic load to the tenant route using 200 rps ramp over 30s, 3) observe new pods stuck in warmup, monitor readiness, kube events, scaledobject metrics. Example k6 command: `k6 run --vus 50 --duration 1m script.js` and model-registry simulated 403 via env var `MODEL_REGISTRY_FAIL=true`.
ops-bot: incident severity set to P1 by marisa at 2026-03-15T12:36Z.
marisa: plan for short-term: kevin to confirm billing auth rollback, shiv to push a rapid canary to increase readiness timeout + reduce KEDA polling, and catie to send customer update. Long-term: add an auth-fast-fail and a prewarm cached snapshot to avoid model-fetch during cold starts.
kevin: I've asked infra to add an emergency temporary KEDA patch: pollingInterval -> 60s, cooldownPeriod -> 90s in prod for the affected namespace. Rolling it in now.
shiv: patch pushed to canary: readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds from 10 -> 30 and prewarm concurrency +1. Also updated container to stop retrying model-fetch on 403 (fail fast). Will monitor logs.
marisa: monitoring dashboards show error rate falling after 12:38 and 504s trending down at 12:42. Customer reporting improved.
catie: customer updated: "latency normalized, thanks for fast response". Closing loop and creating follow-up action items.
marisa: follow-ups: 1) telemetry alert for model-fetch 4xx spikes, 2) KEDA config review to add jittered backoff, 3) add fallback model snapshot for hot routes, 4) run a postmortem. Assigning owners. :white_check_mark:
